post.summary: Plan a swarm: one Haiku task per batch of items (e.g. 1000 7TV emotes in batches of 50), each in code mode with only the read calls in `tools`. Nothing runs until Harmony approves it on approve_url (give Harmony that link); it answers the plan with its cost estimate. mode propose (default) answers { changes } Harmony reviews before they are applied; read answers results; act may call `writes` itself. Follow it with swarm.get or job_status on its job.

mode.description: propose (default): tasks only read and answer { changes }, Harmony reviews them, then they are applied; read: tasks answer results; act: tasks may also call `writes` themselves

items.description: the items to split (at most 5000, JSON at most 512 KB); or give source

source.description: fetch the items server-side now (pages are followed, at most 5000 items)

call.description: a swarm read call, e.g. seventv.set (for a set's emotes: one read gives every name, id and picture; better than searching for each)

path.description: dot path to the list in its answer, e.g. emotes

prompt.description: each task's message; must contain {{items}}; may use {{index}} {{total}} {{count}} {{name}}

tools.description: read calls a task may make: library.list, library.search, library.post, library.about, library.transcript, look, collections.list, links.list, sets.list, names.list, emotes.find, emotes.findMany, seventv.status, seventv.sets, seventv.set, seventv.emote, seventv.owned, seventv.uploads

writes.description: propose: ops a change may name; act: ops a task may call. Any of seventv.rename, seventv.add, seventv.remove, library.title, library.about.set

scope.description: a write whose args have key k must have args[k] in scope[k], e.g. { set_id: ["..."] }

output.description: read/act: the answer's JSON Schema; any mode: the board mapping

schema.description: read/act: each task's answer must match this JSON Schema

board.description: how the answers read on the results board (section 62.4); guessed when left out

prefetch.description: look each item up before its agent starts (section 62.6); the answer is attached to the item (4 KB at most)

call.description: a swarm read call run by the runner (no model) once per item before its agent starts, e.g. emotes.find

args.description: its input; string values may use {{item}} or {{item.path}}, e.g. { "q": "{{item.name}}" }

as.description: the key the answer is attached under on each item, default "lookup"

reduce.description: one final summary over all results

usd.description: the dollar cap, default 1 (at most SWARM_MAX_USD, 10 by default)

stop_after_failed_tasks.description: the swarm stops after this many failed tasks, default 5

get.summary: Unread messages from the agents of your swarms (questions and reports), oldest first, at most 100; they are marked read. Answer a question with swarm.send.
One swarm: status, tasks done/running/failed, dollars spent, the reduce summary, and (propose mode) how many changes are proposed and applied.
One agent of a swarm: its items, status, cost, last steps, result, messages and (propose mode) changes.

post.summary: Harmony applies the kept changes of a propose-mode swarm (no model: each through its op).

skip_clashes.description: untick every kept change with a clash first (the Live Activity's apply)

count.description: how many changes the caller expects to apply (the island's count); 409 when it is not that many

post.summary: Harmony approves a swarm's plan (the web page or a device session); its tasks start.

get.summary: A swarm's results as one board: every agent's outcome and score, and a row per thing its agents answered (title, score, group, other fields, up to 4 media previews). Failed agents appear as a row too. Filter with q, agent, status, group; sort by agent, score or title; pages of up to 200.

schema.description: matches any text of a row (case-insensitive)

get.summary: A propose-mode swarm's proposed changes in task order (a page of up to 200), with what Harmony kept, applied and what clashes.

post.summary: Harmony ticks or edits proposed changes on the review page (a draft until apply).
Harmony declines a swarm's plan; nothing runs.

Message a running swarm's agents: answer an agent's question (to: its number) or tell every agent (to: "all"). It never changes the program: tools, writes, scope, cap and prompt stay what was approved.

woke.description: an agent waiting on a question was woken

get.summary: A swarm's messages, both ways, oldest first (at most 200); does not mark them read.

schema.description: one agent's messages (and those to every agent)

get.summary: A swarm's results in task order (a page of up to 100), each with its error and cost.

post.summary: Run a finished swarm's failed (and skipped) tasks again: it goes back to awaiting Harmony's approval, with a new estimate and a new approve link check.
Stop a swarm: no new tasks start, running ones stop after their current step (or stop applying changes). Nothing is undone.

embedded.description: the meaning has a vector for the current model

pending.description: 7TV still processing the images (usually a minute)

spec_hash.description: the approve and apply POSTs send it back

waiting.description: agents parked on a question to their owner

prefetch.description: looks up each item with this call first (section 62.6)

spec_preview.description: what the approve page shows of the spec

unscoped_writes.description: write ops no scope key limits (none of their input fields is a scope key)

approve_url.description: Harmony approves (and reviews) here; give this link to Harmony

planner.description: who planned it: the client key's name, chat or mcp

score.description: the mean of the ended agents' scores (section 62.3), null before any ended

dir.description: up: an agent to its owner; down: to agents

answered.description: how many of its items appear in its rows

tool_errors.description: calls that still failed after their retries

score.description: 0..1: answered / items × (1 − tool_errors / max(tool_calls, 1)); 0 for a failed agent; null while it runs

start.description: seconds from the start of the clip

words.description: each word's own time (left out for the chat AI)
